choiceTexts: Colloid osmotic pressure of the plasma proteins

answer.line: Blood pressure in the glomerular capillaries pushes water and small solutes into the capsule. It is bulk flow, and it costs no ATP.

steps: Name the forces at the glomerulus. Capillary blood pressure pushes fluid out; plasma proteins and capsule fluid push back.
Look at the plumbing. A wide afferent arteriole in and a narrow efferent one out hold that blood pressure high.
So the push wins. Net filtration is hydrostatic pressure minus the two pull-backs.

choices.text: Colloid osmotic pressure of the plasma proteins
choices.note: The plasma proteins stay in the capillary, and their osmotic pull draws fluid back in. It works against filtration, not for it.
Active transport does its work later, when the tubule reabsorbs. Filtration itself spends no ATP.
Aquaporins are water channels in the collecting duct, set by ADH, far downstream. Nothing called an aquaporin gradient drives filtration.
Capillary blood pressure drives bulk flow into the capsule.
Diffusion moves each solute down its own gradient, as in gas exchange. Filtration pushes water and small solutes through together, in bulk.

lockIt: Filtration is pressure: blood pressure pushes out, plasma proteins pull back, and the push wins.
hook: Wide in, narrow out: pressure stays high.

playWith.label: Nephron lab: tap the glomerulus to see blood pressure push fluid into the capsule

parts.label: Efferent arteriole: narrow, holds the pressure up
Hydrostatic pressure: blood pushes fluid out
Colloid osmotic pressure: plasma proteins pull fluid back
Capsule pressure: filtrate already there pushes back

visual.net: Net filtration: the push out minus both pull-backs

visual.alt: The glomerulus inside Bowman's capsule: a wide afferent arteriole brings blood in and a narrow efferent arteriole carries it out. Thick arrows from the capillary tuft into the capsule, outlined as the answer, show hydrostatic pressure pushing fluid out; thin arrows show the plasma protein pull and capsule pressure pushing back.
visual.caption: Compare the arrow sizes: the push out is the big one, held high by the narrow exit.
